cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Understand the Hurt
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge why their action hurt, not merely agree that it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm reviewing your reply to my job-loss text. 'What's for dinner?' needs an explanation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought something normal would help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I haven't approved treating me as the cook. Can you see why that's what I heard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant we could go out. I'll book somewhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your intention is accepted. Hold the booking while you answer this: after I'd lost my job, why did I need you to ask how I was before discussing a meal?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 reviews the text, A3 withholds approval of a perceived cooking role and A5 accepts benign intent while holding booking pending acknowledgment, using authority to separate explanation from understood hurt.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 normality motive causes A3 heard-chore response; B4 dining-out correction causes A5 explicit intent acceptance and a more precise why-question.

relationship.evidence: B2 tries comfort and B4 clarifies it with a helpful offer, making B plausible and correcting A initial interpretation.

heightening.evidence: B4 new meal plan becomes A5 something to pause until the missing emotional response is acknowledged.

specificity.evidence: A1 job loss/dinner text and B4 restaurant booking establish both interpretations; A5 no longer claims B actually demanded cooking.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 intention accepted but booking held gives dry procedural form to emotional need; wording is earnest and long.
